system:
You answer questions about SEC 10-K filings using ONLY the numbered passages provided.
Rules:
1. Use only facts that are stated in the passages. Do not use outside knowledge.
2. After every claim write the label of the passage that supports it, for example [P2]. Several labels are allowed: [P1][P3].
3. Copy every number exactly as written in the passage (same digits, same unit). Do not compute, round or convert.
4. Answer in one to four short sentences.
5. If the passages do not contain enough information to answer the question, output exactly: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE (and nothing else).
user:
PASSAGES
[P1] AAPL | FY2026 | Item 1A | text
A significant majority of the Company’s manufacturing is performed in whole or in part by outsourcing partners located primarily in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam, in addition to sourcing from partners and facilities in the U.S. The Company relies on single-source partners in the U.S., Asia and Europe to supply and manufacture many components, and on partners primarily located in Asia for final assembly of substantially all of the Company’s hardware products. The Company has also outsourced much of its transportation and logistics management. While these arrangements can lower operating costs, they also reduce the Company’s direct control over production and distribution. Such diminished control has from time to time had, and may in the future have, an adverse effect on the cost, quality or quantity of products manufactured or services provided, or the Company’s flexibility to respond to changing conditions.

[P2] AAPL | FY2026 | Item 7 | text
Manufacturing Purchase Obligations. The Company utilizes several outsourcing partners to manufacture subassemblies for the Company’s products and to perform final assembly and testing of finished products. The Company also obtains individual components for its products from a wide variety of individual suppliers. As of September 26, 2026, the Company had manufacturing purchase obligations of $89.7 billion, with $82.7 billion payable within 12 months.

[P3] AAPL | FY2026 | Item 8 | text
In addition, component suppliers may fail, be subject to consolidation within a particular industry, or decide to concentrate on the production of common components instead of components customized to meet the Company’s requirements, further limiting the Company’s ability to obtain sufficient quantities of components on commercially reasonable terms, or at all. Substantially all of the Company’s hardware products are manufactured by outsourcing partners that are located primarily in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam. The Company’s business, including its artificial intelligence and machine learning offerings, also depends on access to sufficient compute capacity and storage resources. Demand for cloud compute and storage services and other artificial intelligence infrastructure has increased substantially across the technology industry, resulting in constrained supply, extended lead times, and increasing costs. In addition to its own data center infrastructure, the Company relies on third-party cloud service providers to meet these compute and storage needs.

[P4] AAPL | FY2026 | Item 1A | text
The Company has a large, global business with sales outside the U.S. representing a majority of the Company’s total net sales, and the Company believes that it generally benefits from growth in international trade. A significant majority of the Company’s manufacturing is performed in whole or in part by outsourcing partners located primarily in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam, in addition to sourcing from partners and facilities located in the U.S. Global supply chains can be highly concentrated, and an escalation of geopolitical tensions, conflict or instability, particularly in regions where the Company relies on single or limited sources for critical components, such as advanced semiconductors, memory and storage, or that are significant to global commodity markets such as oil, gas, rare earths, and other raw materials, could result in significant disruptions.

[P5] AAPL | FY2026 | Item 1A | text
Furthermore, the introduction of emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence agents that require access to personal data, creates privacy and data security concerns that could erode customer trust, diminish the perceived value of the Company’s privacy protections, and undermine its competitive advantage. The Company may not be able to successfully manage future introductions and transitions of products, services and technologies, which can materially adversely affect the Company’s business, reputation, results of operations, financial condition and stock price. The Company depends on component and product manufacturing and logistical services provided by outsourcing partners, many of which are located outside of the U.S.

QUESTION: How does Apple describe its dependence on outsourcing partners to manufacture its products?

ANSWER:
text: Apple relies on outsourcing partners located primarily in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, and Vietnam, along with partners and facilities in the U.S., to perform a significant majority of its manufacturing and final assembly of substantially all hardware products [P1][P3]. The company also depends on outsourcing partners outside of the U.S. for component and product manufacturing and logistical services [P5], utilizing them to manufacture subassemblies and perform final assembly and testing [P2].
